_about: Reference values for tests/test_aero_subsonic.py. Every value names its source and locator. ANDERSON = J. D. Anderson Jr., Fundamentals of Aerodynamics, 6th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2017 (book page; PDF page of the user's copy = book page + 23). Figure read-offs carry an explicit read tolerance. Values were read from the sources in the session that created this file (2026-10-25).

example_3_17.source: ANDERSON Example 3.17, pp. 279-280 (same flow as Example 3.16)
example_3_17.angle_note: Anderson prints 243.8 and 296.23 deg for the two roots of sin(theta) = -0.897; symmetry about 270 deg requires their sum to be 540, so the printed 296.23 carries a rounding slip of about 0.1 deg; the exact roots are 243.88 and 296.12 deg.

nonlifting_cylinder.source: ANDERSON Eqs. (3.100)-(3.101), pp. 258-259: Cp = 1 - 4 sin^2(theta), from 1 at stagnation to -3 at theta = 90 deg

example_4_5_flat_plate.source: ANDERSON Example 4.5, pp. 355-356 (alpha = 5 deg; Anderson rounds alpha to 0.0873 rad)

example_4_6_naca_23012.source: ANDERSON Example 4.6, pp. 361-364 (mean line written with constants 2.6595, 0.6075, 0.1147, 0.02208 and junction 0.2025; Anderson integrates with rounded intermediate coefficients)

experiment.source: ANDERSON Example 4.6 comparison table p. 364 and Example 4.7 p. 367 (data from Abbott and von Doenhoff via Fig. 4.28)

naca_824_mean_line_theory.source: NACA-TR-824 p. 14 (PDF p. 19), Moment coefficients Example 2 and Angle of zero lift Example 2, Eq. (16); data of the NACA 64 mean line (supplementary figures) scaled linearly
naca_824_mean_line_theory.note: The TR-824 ideal angle 0.74 deg differs from the thin-airfoil integral (1/pi) int dz/dx dtheta = 0.772 deg for the 6-percent 64 mean line by 0.032 deg; recorded as a measured deviation.

naca_2412_experiment.source: ANDERSON Section 4.3 p. 330 (alpha_L=0 = -2.1 deg read from Fig. 4.10, data from Abbott and von Doenhoff) and Example 4.1 pp. 331-332 (c_l = 0.65 at alpha = 4 deg read from Fig. 4.10)

naca_824_lift_slope.source: NACA-TR-824 p. 30 (PDF p. 35): for 6-10 percent thick four-, five-digit and 64-series sections the measured lift-curve slope is very close to 2 pi per rad (0.110 per deg); four-digit zero-lift angles are about 0.93 and 230-series about 1.08 times the thin-airfoil values

naca_1412_ordinates_percent.source: NACA-TR-824 p. 100 (PDF p. 103), table NACA 1412 (stations and ordinates in percent of chord)

tr_537_table_i.source: NACA-TR-537 Table I, p. 522 (PDF p. 2); k2/k1 column is 1e4 x the ratio of the TR-537 formula k2/k1 = (3 (m - p)^2 - m^3)/(1 - m)^3

tr_610_230_camber.source: NACA-TR-610 p. 2 (PDF p. 8): the NACA 230 mean line has a camber of 1.8 percent of the chord at 0.15c

example_3_19.source: ANDERSON Example 3.19, pp. 290-293: eight equal panels on a unit circle, panel 1 the vertical panel facing the stream, numbered clockwise

naca_2412_experiment_comparison.source: Measured (this work) vs ANDERSON p. 330 and Example 4.1 data (see thin_airfoil.naca_2412_experiment); inviscid panel lift slope exceeds the viscous measurement

example_5_1.source: ANDERSON Example 5.1, pp. 457-458: AR = 8, taper 0.8, delta = tau = 0.055 read by Anderson from Fig. 5.20, a0 = 2 pi, alpha = 5 deg

example_5_2.source: ANDERSON Example 5.2, pp. 458-459: rectangular wings, delta = tau, AR 6 (delta 0.055) and AR 10 (delta 0.105), zero-lift angle -2 deg, alpha 3.4 deg, C_D,i = 0.01 at AR 6

figure_5_20.source: ANDERSON Fig. 5.20, p. 452 (McCormick 1979 data): induced drag factor delta vs taper ratio; values digitised from a 300-dpi render of PDF p. 475
figure_5_20.measured_discrepancy: Glauert-series lifting line (this work, a0 = 2 pi, 40 terms) gives delta(taper 1) = 0.0285, 0.0483, 0.0676, 0.0859 for AR 4, 6, 8, 10 and 0.0444 at AR 8, taper 0.8 (Anderson reads 0.055): about 70-80 percent of the figure values. The trend with AR and the location of the minimum agree. Not resolved here; the tests pin the measured ratio band so a change is noticed.
